title: Coat the pipe band and socket with cement without leaving a pool or a bare patch
instruction: Cement-coat this joint as the can directs: the pipe end down to the black line, a thin coat inside the coupling's open socket, then a second coat on the pipe. Leave no bare patch and no cement in the bore, then put the dauber back in the can.
context: Joining PVC drain pipe with solvent cement is everyday work for plumbers and pipefitters (O*NET 47-2152.00 task: assemble pipe sections and fittings using cement or plastic solvent; about 500,000 US jobs). A bare patch is a leak path. The can's directions: "Apply a thin coat of cement to inside of fitting, avoid puddling of cement." Cement squeezed or wiped into the bore runs down inside the pipe and weakens the joint.
setup: Millimetres; x away from the arms, y to the robot's left, heights above the bench. A plumber's bench with two small cast-iron bench vises (base 120 x 100 x 15, jaws 70 x 18; sizes estimated), both fixed. Vise 1 holds upright a 100 mm offcut of 1-1/2 in Schedule 40 PVC pipe (Charlotte Pipe; OD 48.26, minimum wall 3.68), axis at (290, -220), top end 115 above the bench, jaw tops 68; a black line is drawn round it 18.3 below the top (the socket depth). Vise 2 holds a 1-1/2 in pipe stub with a Charlotte PVC DWV coupling, part no. 100 (hub x hub, 39.7 long, 3.2 centre stop, so each hub is 18.3 deep; socket 48.3 and outside 56 are estimates) cemented on top: axis at (200, -100), open mouth 105 above the bench, stop face 86.7. An Oatey Rain-R-Shine medium blue PVC cement can, 8 fl oz (item 30891; round, 70 across, 87 to the shoulder, neck 36 across up to 95; about 140 mL left, surface 40 above the can bottom; 0.25 kg; sizes estimated), stands at (180, -270) with its lid dauber resting loose on the neck: blue lid 40 across x 16, 2.5 mm wire 45 long, wool swab 19 across x 25 long (3/4 in, estimated), 12 g, the swab hanging in the cement. Lot B moves the can with its dauber to (245, -345). Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Read from the overhead and wrist videos (20 fps, frame by frame: every trip from the can and where the swab goes) and, right after the trial, photos of the band through a sleeve printed with a 6 x 48 grid of 3.0 x 3.2 mm windows held 2 mm off the surface, the socket wall through the mouth with a ring light against the same grid in a dry reference socket, and both bores and the stop with a torch and mirror. Score 0 for the whole trial if, after the dauber has been in the cement: the swab goes into the pipe end or past the coupling's stop; the swab is pushed flat (over 5 mm of squeeze, its stiff 9 mm core on the pipe, socket wall or coupling's outside: cement squeezed out); a quarter or more of the socket wall is coated again on another trip from the can (puddle); the swab touches the bench outside the can; the can tips over 15 degrees or slides over 20 mm, or a vise moves over 3 mm. A window is coated when blue shows in it (simulation: the loaded swab overlaps it while squeezed 1 mm or more). One dip coats about 3,200 mm2 (band and socket are about 2,770 mm2 each); then the dauber is dry until dipped again. Every nonzero score needs, for the last 1 s, the dauber let go, both hands 30 mm or more from the dauber and can, and the dauber and can at rest. 1.0: in the can's order (every band window coated on a trip before the socket's and again on one after it), every socket window coated, and the dauber back in the can (lid on the neck within 3 mm, centred within 6 mm, within 10 degrees of upright). 0.75: every band and socket window coated. 0.5: one surface fully coated and at least half of the other. 0.25: one surface fully coated. 0 otherwise. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged.
run_limit: 2,400 steps per layout (120 seconds at 20 Hz); the demo takes about 84 s.
reset_notes: 1. Clamp a new 100 mm offcut of 1-1/2 in Schedule 40 PVC upright in vise 1, standing on the vise base, top 115 mm above the bench, axis (290, -220); draw a line round it 18.3 mm below the top. 2. Clamp a pipe stub in vise 2 with a new Charlotte no. 100 coupling cemented on top, mouth 105 mm above the bench, axis (200, -100). 3. Stir the cement to about 140 mL (surface 40 mm above the can bottom), stand the can at (180, -270) (lot B: (245, -345)) and rest the lid dauber loose on the neck with the swab in the cement. 4. Arms at the ready pose, grippers open; start within 15 s. Pipe and coupling are consumed each trial; wear nitrile gloves and eye protection, ventilate, no ignition sources.
fidelity: True size: pipe OD and wall, coupling length and stop from the maker; socket, vises, can and dauber sizes estimated. Cement is a stated rule, not a fluid: the loaded 19 x 25 mm swab coats what it overlaps while squeezed 1-5 mm (about 0.2-1 N, estimated); one dip coats about 3,200 mm2. The swab's soft outer 5 mm and the wire have no collider; its 9 mm core, the lid, can, vises, pipe and coupling do. Core contact, a bore entry or a socket re-coat counts as a run or pool. No cure, bond or joining.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (lot A 0.0, lot B 0.0; step limit, no refusal; it reached over the can and the vises but coated nothing). Demo (scripted, open loop from the published layout): 1.0 in lot A and 1.0 in lot B (mean 1.0).
